title: the-skills-ask-codemother-who-answers-or-delegates
author: CC (Opus 5), session a187d6ab
owner: codemother owns the face (it is her command surface; ruling 2026-09-06-codemother-owns-the-care-of-the-code); CC builds it; harbor_master keeps the map under delegation; the three SKILL.md edits are tier-2 skill work owned by their charters.
intention: The skills ask codemother for what they need to know about the code — `cairn codemother show artifact <id>` is the first step of /chart, /sorted and /sail — and codemother answers directly or by delegation (the map stays harbor_master's delegated purview, artifacts route to the reader operator_inbox already carries), so `cairn operator` shrinks to what awaits Akien.
why: Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner — codemother owns the care of the code, ruling 2026-09-06-codemother-owns-the-care-of-the-code; a command about the code answered by the operator face has two owners) and Law 1 (a command he could not remember the home of is the resolver spent re-deriving where a settled thing lives).
how: Two arms added to the existing `show` case in cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin/codemother (artifact -> the operator_inbox reader; map -> harbor_master's own show verb, delegated never copied); the three SKILL.md step-0 blocks say `cairn codemother show artifact <id>`; a proof of byte-identity between the codemother and operator verbs over one fixture artifact and of the map arm's exec target; the operator verb's fate and the map breakage's home are open questions on this ticket.
falsifier: RED if, after the build, any of the three skills still names `cairn operator show artifact`; if `cairn codemother show artifact <id>` and `cairn operator show artifact <id>` print different bytes for the same id; if the map verb under codemother does not reach harbor_master's register (a second map is the rival-record failure); or if `cairn operator` gains, rather than loses, a code-facing verb. WRONG-INTENT signal: if the fix copies operator_inbox's reader into codemother instead of delegating — that is the domain box the idea's own author discarded.
traces_to: Law 6 (everything has exactly one owner — codemother owns the care of the code, ruling 2026-09-06-codemother-owns-the-care-of-the-code; a command about the code answered by the operator face has two owners) and Law 1 (a command he could not remember the home of is the resolver spent re-deriving where a settled thing lives).

watchme.enough: ten BUILDME crossings (history.json entries with ticket, dated after this ticket's PROVED, across class-space) with zero triggers — the skills have been asking codemother for ten voyages and she has answered every time
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier: the grep count per skill file, the exit codes of both verbs over the same id, and the BUILDME-crossing count since PROVED
watchme.nexus: cairn/devices/codemother/state.json — the device's standing state beside its code
watchme.consumer: CC at the next /sail (the first line of step 0a: which verb loads the ticket); Akien only when the trigger fires, because a regression here is a skill silently re-homing a command he could not remember the home of

gates_bound: proof gate — cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_codemother_face.py green under the tester in netns; no tooth reads the live commons; the grep tooth reds if any skill reverts to the operator verb.

BUILDME entry gate — intent berth (this cast's), sorted berth, a berthed chart chain claiming the ticket, every bound question answered, AND (fifth lane, physics since 2026-09-15) a clean rehearsal record over the ticket's live bytes — this is a tier-2 ticket and it will be rehearsed under whatever D6 amendment Akien answers on cf80bdb57205.
PROVED exit gate — verdict artifact answering the validate berth's criteria by instrument; then WATCHME(the_skills_stop_asking_the_operator) armed at the probe berth before the crossing.
children: none, because the seam is one shim, one table, three one-line edits, one proof; the only conceivable child — `cairn operator` losing its code-facing verbs — is the alias-or-remove question, and its answer is a decision line on this ticket, not a node
depends_on: cf80bdb57205 PROVED (this ticket's BUILDME rides the fifth lane, so it rehearses under whatever D6 amendment he answers); 5ef041fa162a (.artifact extension) is sequencing only — the reader this face delegates to reads whatever extension the door serves.

decisions.text: Codemother answers every command about the code, directly or by delegation; harbor_master tracks tickets under that delegation and never owns them; `cairn operator` is what awaits Akien.
decisions.by: Akien verbatim 2026-09-15 (review of idea cdb3e93cdfdd): 'code mother answers them all, DIRECTLY OR INDIRECTLY. Harbor master doesn't own the tickets, he just is responsible for tracking them. it's a delegation from one device to another effectively.'

decisions.text: `harbor_master show map` stays harbor_master's; codemother's `show map` delegates to it and never copies it.
decisions.by: Akien verbatim 2026-09-15: 'harbor_master show map should remain harbor_master's delegated purview. if we asked codemother for the same info, it would still come from the harbor_master anyway.'

decisions.text: The face ALREADY EXISTS: `cairn codemother` resolves to cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin/codemother (device dispatch through ~/.cairn/devices/codemother/0/bin), whose `show` verb is a bash case on $what with one arm (dashboard). The build adds two arms, never a new shim: `artifact) exec python3 -m cairn.tools.operator_inbox.inbox show artifact "$@"` and `map) exec "$HOME/.cairn/devices/harbor_master/0/bin/show" map "$@"` (delegation to harbor_master's own show verb, which resolves views through declared_views()); the usage line lists the three.
decisions.by: CC at cast 2026-09-15, CORRECTED the same hour: the first D3 said 'a new bin/cmd/codemother shim' because the census grepped bin/cmd/ and never ran `cairn codemother` — the launcher's device dispatch (bin/cairn:81) already answered. Measured: `cairn codemother show` prints 'usage: cairn codemother show dashboard'.

decisions.text: The three step-0 blocks in skills/chart/SKILL.md, skills/sorted/SKILL.md, skills/sail/SKILL.md say `cairn codemother show artifact <id>`; no other line in the skills names `cairn operator show artifact`.
decisions.by: CC at cast 2026-09-15; measured: exactly three sites (chart:30, sorted:30, sail:23)

decisions.text: Proof at cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_codemother_face.py: byte-identity of `cairn codemother show artifact <id>` and `cairn operator show artifact <id>` over one fixture artifact under CAIRN_COMMONS_ROOT (inbox.py:26, the reader's commons seam) and CAIRN_SKILL_BERTHS pointed at a tempdir (no tooth reads the live commons), the map verb's exec target is harbor_master's own show verb ($HOME/.cairn/devices/harbor_master/0/bin/show map) (asserted on argv, not on live fleet output), and a grep tooth over the three skill files. CONCRETE SHAPE: cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_codemother_face.py is a plain script with four teeth printed as '  ok   <name>' lines (print_teeth_main). The commons seam is CAIRN_COMMONS_ROOT (inbox.py:26 — TICKETS_DIR derives from it; the name 'CAIRN_ARTIFACT_ROOTS' in D5 was the artifact door's seam, not the reader's): a tmp commons with tickets/<12-hex-fixture-id>-fixture.json whose id matches no pending berth, so show_artifact resolves the ticket branch. Tooth 1: subprocess 'cairn codemother show artifact <id>' and subprocess 'python3 -m cairn.tools.operator_inbox.inbox show artifact <id>' under that env both exit 0 and their stdout bytes are equal. Tooth 2: the map arm execs $HOME/.cairn/devices/harbor_master/0/bin/show (an absolute path, so a PATH stub cannot see it): the proof sets HOME to a tmpdir holding .cairn/devices/harbor_master/0/bin/show as a stub that prints its argv, and asserts the argv is ['map', ...] — 'register module' in D5 means this show script, which resolves views through declared_views(); never the Python module directly. Tooth 3: grep over the three SKILL.md files reads 0 'cairn operator show artifact' and 1 'cairn codemother show artifact' each. Tooth 4: 'cairn codemother show' and 'cairn codemother show nope' exit nonzero with a usage line on stderr naming dashboard, artifact and map. FIXTURE TICKET: the fixture ticket is the minimum _format_ticket reads (inbox.py): {"id": "f1e7c0de6b06", "title": "a fixture ticket the face shows", "slug": "a-fixture-ticket-the-face-shows", "node_class": "code-seam", "workflow_and_state": "THINKME -> [TICKETME] -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> PROVED", "falsifier": "the face prints bytes that differ from the operator reader's"} written under the fixture commons root's ticket dir as f1e7c0de6b06-a-fixture-ticket-the-face-shows.json beside an empty question dir — no other field is read by the show path, so none is required

decisions.text: Probe cairn/devices/codemother/probes/the_skills_stop_asking_the_operator.py, armed before WATCHME: trigger = a skill naming the operator verb or the codemother verb exiting nonzero where the operator verb resolves; enough = ten ticket-carrying BUILDME crossings after PROVED with zero triggers. carry(context) returns {operator_mentions: {'skills/<s>/SKILL.md': int grep count of 'cairn operator show artifact' per skill}, codemother_rc: int, operator_rc: int, buildme_crossings_since_proved: int}; enough(context) is buildme_crossings_since_proved >= 10 and not trigger; horizon = 10. CONCRETE SHAPE: cairn/devices/codemother/probes/the_skills_stop_asking_the_operator.py follows cairn/devices/codemother/probes/the_shim_delivers_mail.py exactly — a module-level PROBE = Probe(...) from cairn.tools.base.probe (a frozen dataclass: why, trigger(now, context) -> bool, to='harbor_master', body, carry(context) -> dict, enough(context) -> bool, horizon). carry() measures and returns {'operator_mentions': {<skill file>: <grep count of 'cairn operator show artifact'>}, 'codemother_rc': <exit code of cairn codemother show artifact <id>>, 'operator_rc': <exit code of the operator verb over the same id>, 'buildme_crossings_since_proved': <count of ticket-carrying BUILDME entries in class-space history.json files dated after this ticket's PROVED>}; trigger fires when any mention count is nonzero or codemother_rc != 0 while operator_rc == 0; enough is buildme_crossings_since_proved >= 10 with no trigger. The id carry() reads over is this ticket's own (6b06fcb499fa) — the probe is a live reader by design (it watches the world), unlike the proof, which reads no live commons (D15 of cf80bdb57205). FIELDS AND CONTEXT: body = {"nexus": "hypothesize", "kind": "efficacy", "ticket": "6b06fcb499fa"} — the STATIC part of the poke, same shape as the_shim_delivers_mail.py's body plus this ticket's id; channel is left at its default ('personal'); while_true is left False. context is the dict the codemother shim hands every probe on the pulse (cairn/tools/base/shim.py) — this probe reads NOTHING from it: trigger(now, context), carry(context) and enough(context) each call the module's own _measure(), which greps the three SKILL.md files, runs the two show verbs over 6b06fcb499fa via subprocess, and counts BUILDME entries in every cairn/**/history.json under the repo root (glob 'cairn/**/history.json', not only devices/*) whose 'at' is later than the PROVED entry 'at' in cairn/devices/codemother/history.json for this ticket. The Probe contract is cairn/tools/base/probe.py:303 (frozen dataclass; fields why, trigger, to, channel, body, carry, while_true, enough, horizon). The Probe dataclass's full field list is why, trigger, to, channel, body, carry, while_true, enough, horizon (cairn/tools/base/probe.py:303); this probe sets why, trigger, to, body, carry, enough, horizon and leaves channel and while_true at their defaults.
